newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian central bank warns of inflation pressure.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian central bank warns of inflation pressure.

text.p: Tanzania's annual inflation rate fell to 13.8 percent in February but the central Bank of Tanzania (BoT) warned that further improvements may be hindered by the impact of a recent drought on food prices.

"Despite the positive monetary developments in the recent past, containment of inflation continues to pose a major challenge, particularly now, due to the threatening drought conditions and food shortages which are exerting pressure on food prices," the bank said in a monthly review for February.
The drought ended in March but Tanzania's agricultural sector had been hard hit with many rural communities reporting severe food shortages.

BoT said annual inflation fell to 13.8 percent in February from 14 percent in January but seasonally adjusted inflation during the last six months rose to 15.6 percent in February from 13.4 percent in January.

"The decline in the overall year-to-year inflation is mainly explained by the prevailing tight monetary and fiscal policy stance which has significantly slowed down the expansion in money supply," BoT said.

It forecast annualised inflation to decline to 10 percent by the end of June. It expected an "unsatisfactory food supply situation" to prevail for the remaining period of the 1996/97 fiscal year (July/June).

"Food crop prices are on the increase, reflecting food shortages in the market. The food security department of the ministry of agriculture estimated that the food deficit in the affected areas is about 49,200 tonnes of cereals and 4,920 tonnes of pulses," the bank report said.

To relieve pressure, the bank said the government released 10,000 tonnes of Strategic Grain Reserve (SGR) stocks to the worst drought-affected regions: "Part of the SGR stocks are being redistributed to the open market to stabilise prices."
BoT described as "encouraging" Tanzania's trade account in the reviewed month with a deficit of $26.3 million compared to $33.6 million in January, an improvement of 21.7 percent.
The trade account for February 1997 improved by 23 percent compared with the February 1996 deficit of $34.2 million.

The improvement was due to an increase in export earnings and a decrease in imports. Export earnings for February rose 6.5 percent to $76.4 million compared to the same month in 1996 while imports fell three percent to $102.7 million.
With the exception of coffee and cotton, commodity prices remained stable in the month. Coffee prices recovered slightly averaging $1.6 per/kg compared to $1.5 per/kg in January.

The BoT attributed the rise to "speculative demand increases following indications that the coffee crop in Brazil for the 1997/98 production season is expected to be below 20 million 60-kg bags against a market consensus of 23-24 million."
At the end of February, Tanzania's external debt stood at $7.58 billion. BoT gave no figures for debt servicing.
